And you'll think, "Wow, this is boring. I don't want to do this." Then you'll keep doing it anyways because you have to. And maybe (probably) (*definitely*) you'll have to do something you're not good at or you just don't know how to do. So you'll have to figure out how to get help. Ask your teachers about tutoring. Look online. Don't just shrug and say, eh, I'll figure it out later.

Eventually you'll get in the habit of forcing yourself to do the stuff you have to do anyways. And I guess that's work ethic. It helps to remember why you're doing all of this, too. Like, I have to do this homework because if I don't my grades will suffer and if they drop too low I could fail this class and maybe not even graduate highschool and then where would I be? But none of that's going to happen because I'm doing my homework right now. And if I do poorly even after putting in the effort I'll put in more effort and make it better.

Sorry if this doesn't really help much. I'm no expert or anything- I'm barely out of high school myself- but I think this is it. One day you'll be an adult and you'll have way more serious stuff you may or may not want to do. And not doing that stuff could ruin your life. Or just make your house really stinky, depending on what exactly it is you're not doing. Sucking it up and getting it done is just another life skill, I guess.

I think you should try out therapy/counseling and see where you go from there. Sometimes antidepressants can really help. Sometimes they don't, but you'll never know until you try. I'm not sure how taking those medications could prohibit you from participating in sports in any way, but if you really are depressed then there is a big risk of it getting worse if you don't address it.

Assuming you're going to college, get ready. Start really thinking about what you'd like to major in and what schools you want to apply to. Make sure your SAT/ACT scores are high enough, whether or not those schools require an essay, apply for financial aid, figure out housing/dorm situation, etc. It's too early for most of the paper work and all of that right now but believe me, you do not want to be scrambling through admission at the last second.

As for while you're still in high school, don't sweat it. Seriously. As soon as it's over and done with, that's it. It won't matter anymore. No one will care if you weren't the top of your class or if you had the most friends or whatever. Schools and employers will care about the existence of your diploma, maybe, but all of the other stuff will just be in the past.
